subject: Co-tenancy impact assessment & next steps for HealthX
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@healthx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-01T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + a small ask on co-tenancy concerns

Hi Emma — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the one piece we need to move the evaluation forward:

Summary from our side:
- Primary ask: HealthX needs guidance on whether Hosted API will meet your isolation/SLO requirements or whether Dedicated/Private is required for initial launch.
- Key constraints you mentioned: HIPAA-adjacent data handling, predictable 95th-pct latency < 250ms for inference at 50qps, and tolerance for noisy-node variability < 5% of tail latency.

Ask: could you share a short traffic-profile CSV (sample TPS/qps distribution and peak window) and confirm whether customer data touches PHI fields in prompts or only hashed IDs? I attached a blank template to make it easy.

Next steps I propose:
1) You drop the traffic-profile and call out PHI/hashed fields.
2) Our infra team (Marissa) will run a co-tenancy impact summary mapping expected tail risk and fallback options.
3) We follow with a 30-minute tech sync next week to walk the summary and pricing delta for Dedicated/Private if needed.

Attachments: prod-traffic-profile.csv (template)

Thanks — Ben

From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@healthx.com>

Date: 2027-09-02T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + a small ask on co-tenancy concerns

Ben — thanks for the clear note. Attached is the traffic export and a top-level note on our data shape.

Files attached: HealthX-traffic-aug.csv, HealthX-data-shape.txt

Short answers:
- PHI: We do not send raw PHI to vendors. Prompts include hashed patient IDs and de-identified clinical notes (structured) today. We may need to send limited clinical snippets later in pilot; that is why we are cautious about isolation.
- Peak: 60 qps sustained for short bursts (30-60s) during business hours, baseline 8-12 qps off-peak.

We are open to starting on Hosted if you recommend mitigations (strict routing, KV-prefix caching, SLA escape hatch). But we need a clear playbook for if tail latency or noisy-instance incidents happen.

—Emma

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-02T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: co-tenancy risk sketch for HealthX (draft)

Ben / Vanessa — I sketched an initial risk matrix based on Emma's numbers. Highlights: 

- With baseline ~10 qps and 60 qps peaks (short bursts), the main risk on Hosted is tail spikes when other tenants push long-context loads. That can increase 95th-pct by ~15-30% depending on kernel selection and KV cache hit rate.
- Mitigations we can offer from Hosted without Dedicated:
  * Strict model routing to a faster LLM variant for HealthX routes only (higher cost but better tail).
  * Prefix KV caching + pre-warm on predicted peak windows (we can coordinate cron triggers).
  * Autoscale burst capacity alarms with guaranteed warm workers for enterprise customers (configurable, short warm-up SLA).
- When to recommend Dedicated/Private: if HealthX plans to send identifiable clinical snippets or requires guaranteed <250ms 95th for 50qps sustained; Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools and SLA-backed latency.

Pricing note: a short Dedicated commitment would add an estimated 20-30% uplift vs higher-cost Hosted variants when tuned for isolation. Private/VPC adds additional onboarding and support costs.

I'll turn this into a one-pager and bring the perf numbers from our runtime bench next. Want to make sure we surface the fallback playbook explicitly (Hosted with escape to Dedicated + webhook alerts).

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@healthx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-03T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps and tech sync — Wed Sep 8 or Thu Sep 9?

Emma — thanks for the upload and the clear constraints. Quick reply and scheduling: 

1) We recommend a two-phase approach to minimize cost and mitigate risk:
   - Phase A (Pilot on Hosted): Begin on Hosted API with strict route isolation + faster-variant routing and prefix caching. Configure an autoscale warm pool during your business hours and a webhook-based incident responder. This gets you fast time-to-value.
   - Phase B (Commit to Dedicated if/when): If during a 2–4 week pilot we see sustained tail incidents or you need identifiable snippets handled, we move to Dedicated or Private VPC. We'll define explicit SLO thresholds and a runbook for failover.

2) Action items:
   - HealthX: confirm if any prompts will include clinical snippets during pilot (Emma) — yes/no.
   - Redwood: Marissa will produce the co-tenancy impact one-pager (includes bench-derived tail delta, recommended routing, and estimated cost uplift).
   - Scheduling: propose Wed Sep 8 10:30am PT or Thu Sep 9 9:00am PT — 30 minutes technical sync.

3) Attachments I uploaded for your review: HealthX-Security-Questionnaire.pdf (we filled standard answers for the pilot) and the prod-traffic-profile.csv you started.

If Wed works, I'll send a calendar invite with an agenda (benchmarks, routing config, rollback plan).

Best — Ben
